answer: In a PoA attestation graph, trust propagates through bounded-length random walks, so each verifier’s signal is weighted by reachable, independently attested mass rather than identities alone. A sybil cluster may harbor many nodes, but if its external cut has low conductance, few walk transitions cross it; spectral mixing and min-cut transitivity therefore bound its aggregate voting weight, revealing concentrated influence through a prism of cross-checks.
